text: The provisions of the Regulation shall not apply to parts of the external surface which, with the vehicle laden and all doors, windows and access lids closed, are at a height of more than 2 metres.
condition: part at a height of more than 2 m

text: The provisions of the Regulation shall not apply to parts of the external surface which, with the vehicle laden and all doors, windows and access lids closed, are below the floor line.
condition: part below the floor line

text: The provisions of the Regulation shall not apply to parts of the external surface which, in their static condition as well as when in operation, cannot be contacted by a sphere 100 mm in diameter.
condition: part not contactable by a 100 mm sphere

text: The external surface of vehicles shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any pointed or sharp parts or any projections of such shape, dimensions, direction or hardness as to be likely to increase the risk or seriousness of bodily injury to a person hit by the external surface or brushing against it in the event of a collision.
The external surface of vehicles shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any part likely to catch on pedestrians, cyclists or motor cyclists.
No protruding part of the external surface shall have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm.
condition: part protrudes 5 mm or more

text: Parts of the external surface which protrude less than 5 mm shall have their outward facing angles blunted, save where such parts protrude less than 1.5 mm.
condition: part protrudes less than 5 mm but not less than 1.5 mm

text: Protruding parts of the external surface may have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm only if made of a material of hardness not exceeding 60 Shore A.
condition: radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm

text: The hardness measurement shall be taken with the component as installed on the vehicle.
Where it is impossible to carry out a hardness measurement by the Shore A procedure, comparable measurements shall be used for evaluation.
condition: Shore A measurement impossible

text: The provisions of paragraphs 5.1 to 5.5 shall apply in addition to the particular specifications of paragraph 6, except where these particular specifications expressly provide otherwise.

Added ornaments which project more than 10 mm from their support shall retract, become detached or bend over under a force of 10 daN exerted at their most salient point in any direction in a plane approximately parallel to the surface on which they are mounted.
condition: ornament projects more than 10 mm, not on a radiator grille

text: Ornaments on radiator grilles shall meet only the general requirements of paragraph 5.
condition: ornament on radiator grille

text: The 10 daN force on ornaments shall be applied with a flat-ended ram of not more than 50 mm diameter; where this is not possible, an equivalent method shall be used.
After the ornaments are retracted, detached or bent over, the remaining projections shall not project more than 10 mm.
The remaining projections after the ornaments are retracted, detached or bent over shall in any case satisfy paragraph 5.2.
If an ornament is mounted on a base, the base shall be regarded as belonging to the ornament and not to the supporting surface.
condition: ornament mounted on a base

text: Protective strips or shielding on the external surface, although not subject to paragraph 6.1.1, shall be firmly secured to the vehicle.
Projecting visors and rims on headlights shall not project more than 30 mm, measured in relation to the external transparent surface of the headlight.
condition: headlight fitted with projecting visors or rims

text: Projecting visors and rims on headlights shall have a radius of curvature of at least 2.5 mm throughout.
condition: headlight fitted with projecting visors or rims

text: For a headlamp mounted behind an additional transparent surface, the projection of visors and rims shall be measured from the outermost transparent surface.
condition: headlamp behind an additional transparent surface

text: The projections of headlight visors and rims shall be determined according to the method in Annex 3 paragraph 3.
Retracting headlights shall meet the provisions of paragraph 6.2.1 in both the operative and retracted positions.
condition: retracting headlights

text: Paragraph 6.2.1 does not apply to headlamps sunk into or overhung by the bodywork, provided the bodywork complies with paragraph 6.9.1.
condition: headlamp sunk into or overhung by the bodywork

text: Paragraph 5.4 shall not apply to gaps between fixed or movable elements, including those of air intake or outlet grilles and radiator grilles, provided that the distance between consecutive elements does not exceed 40 mm and the grilles and gaps have a functional purpose.
For grille and gap elements with gaps of between 40 mm and 25 mm, the radii of curvature shall be 1 mm or more.
condition: distance between consecutive elements between 40 mm and 25 mm

text: If the distance between two consecutive grille or gap elements is equal to or less than 25 mm, the radii of curvature of external faces of the elements shall not be less than 0.5 mm.
condition: distance between consecutive elements ≤ 25 mm

text: The distance between two consecutive elements of grilles and gaps shall be determined according to the method in Annex 3 paragraph 4.
The junction of the front with the side faces of each element forming a grille or gap shall be blunted.
The wiper shaft shall be furnished with a protective casing which has a radius of curvature meeting paragraph 5.4.
condition: applies also to rear window wipers and headlamp wipers

text: The protective casing of the wiper shaft shall have an end surface area of not less than 150 mm².
condition: applies also to rear window wipers and headlamp wipers

text: The wiper holder (head and main part) shall be designed with a radius of curvature meeting paragraph 5.4.
condition: applies also to rear window wipers and headlamp wipers

text: Rounded covers of wipers shall have a minimum projected area of 150 mm² when measured not more than 6.5 mm from the point projecting furthest.
condition: rounded covers; applies also to rear window wipers and headlamp wipers

text: Wiper blades, supporting members, second holder, functional hinge between holder head and holder, and junction between main and second holder, although exempt from paragraph 5.4, shall be so made as to have no sharp angles or pointed or cutting parts.
Compliance with paragraphs 6.4.1 and 6.4.2 shall be verified with the wipers in parked position.

The ends of the bumpers shall be turned in towards the external surface in order to minimize the risk of fouling; this is satisfied if the bumper is recessed or integrated within the bodywork, or the bumper end is turned in so that it is not contactable by a 100 mm sphere and the gap between bumper end and surrounding bodywork does not exceed 20 mm.

If the line of the bumper corresponding to the outline contour of the car vertical projection is on a rigid surface, that surface shall have a minimum radius of curvature of 5 mm at all its points from the contour line to 20 mm inward, within the zone between and in front (or rear for rear bumper) of the tangential points of two vertical planes at 15° to the longitudinal plane of symmetry.
condition: bumper contour line on a rigid surface

text: The rigid bumper surface shall have a minimum radius of curvature of 2.5 mm in all other cases.
condition: bumper contour line on a rigid surface

text: Parts on or of the bumper or bumper insets with a projection of less than 5 mm, such as joint covers and headlamp washer jets, though exempt from 6.5.2, shall have their outward facing angles blunted, save where they protrude less than 1.5 mm.
condition: projection less than 5 mm but not less than 1.5 mm

text: The bumper cover is not subject to paragraph 6.5.2 but shall comply with the provisions of paragraph 5.
The projection of door or luggage compartment handles shall not exceed 40 mm.
The projection of hinges and push-buttons of doors, luggage compartments and bonnets, and of fuel tank filler caps and covers, shall not exceed 30 mm.
Lateral door handles which rotate parallel to the plane of the door shall have their open end directed towards the rear.
condition: lateral door handles rotating parallel to the door plane

text: The end of lateral door handles rotating parallel to the plane of the door shall be turned back towards the plane of the door and fitted into a protective surround or be recessed.
condition: lateral door handles rotating parallel to the door plane

text: Lateral door handles which pivot outwards in any direction not parallel to the door plane shall, when in the closed position, be enclosed in a protective surround or be recessed.
condition: handles pivoting outwards not parallel to the door plane

text: The open end of outward-pivoting lateral door handles shall face either rearwards or downwards, unless conditions (a) to (d) are met.
condition: handles pivoting outwards not parallel to the door plane

text: Outward-pivoting door handles whose open end does not face rearwards or downwards shall have an independent return mechanism.
condition: open end not facing rearwards or downwards

text: Outward-pivoting door handles whose open end does not face rearwards or downwards shall not project more than 15 mm should the return mechanism fail.
condition: open end not facing rearwards or downwards

text: Outward-pivoting door handles whose open end does not face rearwards or downwards shall comply, in the opened position, with paragraph 5.4.
condition: open end not facing rearwards or downwards

text: Outward-pivoting door handles whose open end does not face rearwards or downwards shall have an end surface area, measured not more than 6.5 mm from the point projecting furthest, of not less than 150 mm2.
condition: open end not facing rearwards or downwards

text: Paragraph 5.4 shall not apply to wheels, wheel nuts, hub caps and wheel discs.
The wheels, wheel nuts, hub caps and wheel discs shall not exhibit any pointed or sharp projections that extend beyond the external plane of the wheel rim.
Wing nuts shall not be allowed.

When the vehicle is travelling in a straight line, no part of the wheels other than the tyres situated above the horizontal plane through their axis of rotation shall project beyond the vertical projection, in a horizontal plane, of the external surface or structure.

Wheel discs covering wheel and hub nuts may project beyond the vertical projection of the external surface or structure only if functional requirements so warrant, the radius of curvature of the projecting surface is not less than 30 mm and the projection in no case exceeds 30 mm.
condition: wheel disc projecting beyond the vertical projection of the external surface

text: Sheet-metal edges, such as gutter edges and the rails of sliding doors, shall not be permitted unless they are folded back (by approximately 180°, or towards the bodywork so they cannot be contacted by a 100 mm sphere) or are fitted with a shield meeting the applicable requirements of the Regulation.

Paragraph 5.4 shall not apply to the rear edge of the bonnet (including its lateral extrapolation up to the outermost lateral point of the windscreen glass) and the front edge of the rear luggage boot.
Folds in body panels may have a radius of curvature of less than 2.5 mm only if it is not less than one-tenth of the height H of the projection, measured by the method of Annex 3 paragraph 1.
condition: radius of curvature of fold less than 2.5 mm

text: Lateral air or rain deflectors shall have a radius of curvature of at least 1 mm on edges capable of being directed outwards.
Jacking brackets shall not project more than 10 mm beyond the vertical projection of the floor line lying vertically above them.

Exhaust pipes shall not project more than 10 mm beyond the vertical projection of the floor line lying vertically above them, unless they terminate in rounded edges with a minimum radius of curvature of 2.5 mm.
Air intake and outlet flaps shall meet the requirements of paragraphs 5.2, 5.3 and 5.4 in all positions of use.
Opening roofs shall be considered only in the closed position.
condition: opening roof

text: Convertible vehicles shall be examined with the hood in both the raised and lowered positions.
condition: convertible vehicles

text: With the hood lowered, no examination shall be made of the vehicle inside an imaginary surface formed by the hood when in the raised position.
condition: convertible with hood lowered

text: Where a cover for the linkage of the folded hood is provided as standard equipment, the examination shall be made with the cover in position.
condition: hood linkage cover provided as standard equipment

text: Windows which move outwards from the external surface shall, in all positions of use, have no exposed edge facing forwards.
condition: windows moving outwards

text: No part of a window which moves outwards from the external surface shall, in any position of use, project beyond the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
condition: windows moving outwards

text: Registration plate supporting brackets provided by the vehicle manufacturer shall comply with paragraph 5.4 if they are contactable by a 100 mm diameter sphere when a registration plate is fitted per the manufacturer's recommendation.
condition: bracket contactable by a 100 mm sphere with plate fitted

text: Luggage racks and ski racks shall be so attached to the vehicle that positive locking exists in at least one direction.

Luggage racks and ski racks shall be attached so that horizontal, longitudinal and transverse forces at least equal to the vertical load-bearing capacity specified by the rack manufacturer can be transmitted.
For the test of the luggage rack or ski rack fixed to the vehicle according to the manufacturer's instructions, the test loads shall not be applied at one point only.

Surfaces of luggage or ski racks which, after installation, can be contacted by a 165 mm diameter sphere shall not have parts with a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm, unless paragraph 6.3 can be applied.

Fastening elements of luggage or ski racks, such as bolts tightened or loosened without tools, shall not project more than 40 mm beyond the surfaces referred to in 6.16.2, determined per Annex 3 paragraph 2 but using a 165 mm sphere where the method of Annex 3 paragraph 2.2 is employed.
condition: fastening elements operable without tools

text: Radio receiving and transmitting aerials shall be fitted so that, if their unattached end is less than 2 m from the road surface in any position of use specified by the aerial manufacturer, it is inside the zone bounded by vertical planes 10 cm inside the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
condition: unattached end less than 2 m from the road surface

text: Aerials shall be so fitted, and if necessary their unattached ends so restricted, that no part of the aerials protrudes beyond the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
The unattached ends of aerial shafts shall be fitted with fixed cappings with radii of curvature not less than 2.5 mm.
The bases of aerials shall not project more than 40 mm when determined according to Annex 3 paragraph 2.
condition: aerial not located behind the driver's R point transverse plane with projection ≤ 70 mm

text: Where the base of an aerial cannot be identified due to absence of a flexible shaft or part, after a horizontal force of not more than 50 daN in forward and rearward direction applied by a flat-ended ram of not more than 50 mm diameter at its most salient part, the aerial shall either bend towards the support and not project more than 40 mm, or break off leaving no sharp or dangerous part contactable by the 100 mm sphere and not projecting more than 40 mm.
condition: aerial base cannot be identified

text: Aerials located behind the vertical transverse plane through the driver's R point are exempt from 6.17.4 and 6.17.4.1 provided the maximum projection of the aerial including its housing does not exceed 70 mm, determined per Annex 3 paragraph 2.
condition: aerial behind the driver's R point transverse plane

text: Aerials located behind the vertical transverse plane through the driver's R point which project more than 70 mm shall meet paragraph 6.17.4.1 using a projection limit of 70 mm instead of 40 mm.
condition: aerial behind the driver's R point plane projecting more than 70 mm

text: Luggage racks, ski racks and radio aerials approved as separate technical units shall not be offered for sale, sold or purchased unless accompanied by assembly instructions.
condition: approved as separate technical units

text: The assembly instructions shall contain sufficient information to enable the approved components to be mounted on the vehicle in a manner that complies with the relevant provisions of paragraphs 5 and 6.
The assembly instructions for telescopic aerials shall indicate the positions of use.
condition: telescopic aerials

text: Vehicles and separate technical units approved under this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements of paragraphs 5 and 6.
Suitable controls of the production shall be carried out to verify that the requirements of paragraph 8.1 are met.
The holder of the approval shall ensure the existence of procedures for the effective control of the quality of products.
The holder of the approval shall have access to the control equipment necessary for checking the conformity to each approved type.
The holder of the approval shall ensure that test result data are recorded and related documents remain available for a period determined in accordance with the Type Approval Authority.
The holder of the approval shall analyse the results of each type of test to verify and ensure the stability of the product characteristics, making allowance for variation of industrial production.
The holder of the approval shall ensure that for each type of product at least the tests prescribed in Annex 3 are carried out.

The holder of the approval shall ensure that any sampling giving evidence of non-conformity gives rise to another sampling and another test, and all necessary steps shall be taken to re-establish conformity of the corresponding production.
condition: non-conformity found

text: The Type Approval Authority which granted type approval may at any time verify the conformity control methods applicable to each production unit.
In every inspection, the test books and production survey records shall be presented to the visiting inspector.

The inspector may take samples at random to be tested in the manufacturer's laboratory; the minimum number of samples may be determined according to the results of the manufacturer's own verification.

When the quality level appears unsatisfactory or the validity of tests under 8.4.2 needs verification, the inspector shall select samples to be sent to the Technical Service which conducted the type approval tests.
condition: quality level unsatisfactory or test validity to be verified

text: The Type Approval Authority may carry out any test prescribed in this Regulation.
The normal frequency of inspections authorized by the Type Approval Authority shall be one per two years.
Where negative results are recorded during an inspection, the Type Approval Authority shall ensure that all necessary steps are taken to re-establish conformity of production as rapidly as possible.
condition: negative results recorded

text: In the approval mark arrangements (Model A and Model B), the dimension 'a' shall be at least 8 mm.

The height H of a projection of folds in body panels is determined graphically by reference to the circumference of a 165 mm diameter circle, internally tangential to the external outline of the external surface at the section to be checked.

H is the maximum value of the distance, measured along a straight line passing through the centre of the 165 mm diameter circle, between the circumference of the circle and the external contour of the projection of the body panel fold.

Where a 100 mm diameter circle cannot contact externally part of the external outline of the external surface at the section under consideration, the surface outline in this area is assumed to be that formed by the circumference of the 100 mm diameter circle between its tangent points with the external outline.
condition: if it is not possible for a 100 mm diameter circle to contact externally part of the external outline at the section under consideration

text: Drawings of the necessary sections through the external surface shall be provided by the manufacturer to allow the height of the projections of folds in body panels to be measured.

The dimension of the projection of a component mounted on a convex surface may be determined either directly or by reference to a drawing of an appropriate section of this component in its installed condition.
condition: if the component is mounted on a convex surface

text: If the dimension of the projection of a component mounted on a surface other than convex cannot be determined by simple measurement, it shall be determined by the maximum variation of the distance of the centre of a 100 mm diameter sphere from the nominal line of the panel when the sphere is moved over and is in constant contact with that component.
condition: if the component is mounted on a surface other than convex and the projection cannot be determined by simple measurement

text: The projection of headlamp visors and rims from the external surface of the headlamp shall be measured horizontally from the point of contact of a 100 mm diameter sphere as shown in Figure 4.

The dimension of a gap or space between elements of a grille shall be determined by the distance between two planes passing through the points of contact of the sphere and perpendicular to the line joining those points of contact.
